 BASKETBALL Philadelphia 76ers Where to watch Philadelphia 76ers vs Chicago Bulls and what time does this Monday's game start?
 Philadelphia, leaders of the East, host the free-falling Bulls at the Wells Fargo Center
 Philadelphia 76ers' LeBron James looks on during the second half of an NBA Cup basketball game against the New York Knicks, Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, in Philadelphia. (AP Photo/Chris Szagola) Chris Szagola

 There are games in which the schedule seems like a whim, and this is one of them. The Philadelphia 76ers, owners of the best start in the Eastern Conference, open the doors of the Wells Fargo Center to a Chicago Bulls team that can't find its footing.
 The contrast could not be sharper: Philadelphia arrives looking every bit a contender, while Chicago tries to stop a bleeding that already has it at the bottom of the league.
 LeBron James sticks his tongue out at two young fans asking for a high five Where to watch the Sixers vs Bulls game and what time does it start?
 The game will be played this Monday, November 2, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. Eastern Time (Central European Time), at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, a venue with a capacity of 20,478 fans.
 For the U.S. audience, the local broadcast of the game depends on each team's market: in Philadelphia it will be on NBC Sports Philadelphia and, in Chicago, it can be watched on Chicago Sports Network.
 Overall, the game between the Sixers and the Bulls will be broadcast with NBA League Pass as a complementary streaming option.
 Philadelphia 76ers, with a leader's identity
 The 76ers lead the Eastern Conference with a 6-1 record in seven games played, the best winning record in the East and one of the three best in the entire league. In the overall standings, they occupy third place among the 30 franchises.
 Their recent streak supports the optimism. Philadelphia is coming off a run of significant wins: they won at the home of the New York Knicks, defeated Cleveland and Milwaukee at the Wells Fargo Center, and recently recorded two straight road victories against Indiana and Charlotte.
 The only stumble in that stretch was a home loss to Detroit, a reminder that the only opponent to have beaten them is also battling at the top.
 The team leading this roster brings together a rare mix of veteran experience and young talent: Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey as the backbone, with Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, and shooting guard Anfernee Simons providing offensive firepower, along with young Bahamian point guard VJ Edgecombe, just 21 years old.
 It is a rotation capable of scoring in waves, something a defensively fragile opponent should fear.
 Chicago Bulls, looking to stop the slide
 The Bulls' outlook is the opposite. With a 1-5 record, Chicago sinks to 26th place in the overall standings and sits fourth in the Central Division, ahead of only Milwaukee. Their point differential is among the most worrying in the East, a symptom of a team that gives up too much: 776 points allowed in six games.
 Their recent run is nightmarish. After being blown out in Toronto, they earned their only win of the season in Milwaukee, but since then they have piled up three straight losses: at home against Washington (120-124), a rout in Boston, and another painful setback against the Knicks. The pattern is clear: when Chicago scores, it also allows scoring without restraint.
 The roster, though, has some interesting young pieces. Australian point guard Josh Giddey is the creative engine, with shooter Buddy Hield, shooting guard Norman Powell, playmaker Tre Jones, and promising Lithuanian forward Matas Buzelis rounding out a core that points more to the future than the present.
 Inside, Nic Claxton and Zach Collins carry the responsibility in the paint, precisely the area where Embiid can do damage.
 Implications in the Eastern Conference standings
 For the 76ers, a win would solidify their lead in the East and keep them tied in victories with the league’s best in this early stretch. They also sit atop the Atlantic Division, ahead of Boston. It is not a game in which they can afford to relax, but it is one in which everything points to them needing to capitalize.
 For the Bulls, each loss carries double weight in an increasingly crowded lower tier. They share the bottom of the East with Milwaukee, and only Brooklyn and, overall, Sacramento remain below them. Picking up points in Philadelphia would be almost a feat, but avoiding another blowout would already be a first step toward stopping the spiral.
 76ers vs Bulls Prediction
 The numbers and the form point in one direction only. Philadelphia is playing at home, comes in on a roll, has the decisive advantage in the paint, and faces an opponent that gives up too easily.
 The logical outcome is a clear victory for the 76ers; the only real question is whether Chicago can keep the score competitive or if it turns into another long night for a franchise urgently seeking its second bit of joy of the season.
